name: ALERT Radio Setup
tagline: Front door for Quansheng ALERT receivers: setup guide, browser installer for both radio families, firmware refreshed weekly.
about: The one link to give anyone who wants a Quansheng handheld that decodes ALERT flood telemetry. It has a setup guide (what to buy, which radio you have, every screen, key and setting, logging to a computer), a Chrome/Edge Web Serial installer that backs up and flashes both the UV-K5 V3 / UV-K1 and the older UV-K5, and the firmware itself, rebuilt from source every week. It holds no firmware source of its own.

components.name: Setup guide
components.what: One page: what ALERT is, what to buy, how to tell a V3 from a UV-K5, installing, every screen, key and setting, logging, troubleshooting, downloads.

components.name: Browser installer
components.what: Wizard that reads the bootloader, refuses firmware for the other chip, backs the radio up, flashes it and checks the result.

components.name: Bootloader protocol
components.what: Framing, obfuscation, image checks and commands for both bootloaders (2.x and 7.x), checked against serialtool and k5prog vectors.

components.name: Web Serial transport
components.what: Talks to the radio over Web Serial: backup, restore and flash for both families, including the V3's USB-C port that changes id.

components.name: Published firmware
components.what: The V3 build and the UV-K5 builds, with a manifest giving each one's size, sha256, station count and source commit.

components.name: Weekly firmware refresh
components.what: Every Monday (or on dispatch) copies the UV-K5 builds, compiles the V3 build reproducibly, rewrites the manifest and commits only real changes.

components.name: Cable tools
components.what: A guide to building a two-pin programming cable and k5diag.py, a command-line cable and radio check.

components.name: Tests
components.what: Protocol vectors, the whole installer driven against simulated radios of both kinds, the guide page, and the manifest check.

provides.name: Setup guide and installer
provides.what: The one link for setting up a radio; the V3 and UV-K5 firmware READMEs send people here, and to /flash/?radio=v3 or v1.

provides.name: Published firmware and manifest
provides.what: Current builds for both families; manifest.json lists each file with its sha256, size, station count and source commit. Served at firmware/manifest.json under the site once Pages serves /docs.

provides.name: firmware-updated dispatch
provides.what: A repository_dispatch of type firmware-updated rebuilds and republishes straight away instead of waiting for Monday.

consumes.what: The UV-K5 V3 / UV-K1 ALERT firmware, compiled here (RescueOps, -DENABLE_ALERT=ON) into docs/firmware/v3/.
consumes.on_change: Nothing by hand, so no drift issue: refresh-firmware.yml rebuilds it every Monday 03:17 UTC and on a firmware-updated dispatch, committing only if the bytes change. To publish sooner: gh workflow run refresh-firmware.yml --ref main -R cdomotor-g/quansheng_alert_ALL.

consumes.what: The UV-K5 builds quansheng_alert publishes in its docs/firmware/, copied as they are into docs/firmware/v1/.
consumes.on_change: Nothing by hand, so no drift issue: the same weekly refresh copies them. quansheng_alert is archived, so they no longer change.

consumes.what: Screen captures of the V3 receiver, copied into docs/img/screens/ for the guide.
consumes.on_change: Copy the new or changed PNGs into docs/img/screens/ and check the guide's captions.

consumes.what: The guide's account of the V3 receiver: screens, keys, settings, the 443 built-in stations, and logging with alertterm.py.
consumes.on_change: Re-read the guide's V3 screens, keys, settings and logging sections against the change and update them.

consumes.what: The UV-K5 installer and cable page, extended here to both radio families.
consumes.on_change: Nothing: taken once and now independent; quansheng_alert is archived.

consumes.what: k5diag.py, the command-line cable and radio check, a verbatim copy.

asks.what: After a push to main, send quansheng_alert_ALL a firmware-updated repository dispatch (needs a token secret), so a new build is published that day, not the next Monday.
